scientific_integrity: All three cases are proved analytically. A common top-vector occurrence proves the all-top case; a coordinate-maximizing index selected independently of the remaining coordinate arrays gives the sharp positive lower bound; and a rare-upper-tail diagonal inequality establishes necessity even for arbitrary atomic distributions. The exact finite verifier is a replay check only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes iid vector samples with independent, possibly heterogeneous, one-dimensional coordinates and fixed finite dimension. It characterizes positive liminf leader probability, not full convergence when at least two marginal top atoms are absent. Under one exceptional marginal with ties only the uniform lower bound is asserted. Related results under argmax-intersection or occupancy terminology may exist.
title: Terminal atoms exactly classify leaders of heterogeneous product samples
